answer: A Sybil brake in an AI-agent economy is a slashable bond tied to every attestation: an agent must lock stake before it may vouch for peers, and each vouch is scored against an independently attested graph. To fake a sonnet of identities, an attacker must fund a real bond per account, and once any colluding umber is uncovered, the stake behind it is slashed in full. The cost of one extra fake identity is therefore the bond plus the expected loss when the planted reef is detected, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents merely expose capital.
